ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, shareholders, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and registered agents against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, HM Treasury sanctions lists, Interpol Red Notices, and the RMI domestic conduct/financial-services watchlist. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family and close associates, and for any person from a high-risk third country identified by FATF. Results must be documented in a written screening report, kept with the registered agent, and made available to the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations – Corporate Name Reservation Portal (submitted exclusively through licensed Marshall Islands registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate record language is English. Proposed names must be submitted in Latin-alphabet English characters only. Non-Roman script transliterations, if any, must be accompanied by a notarized English translation. Names must be distinct, non-deceptive, and not confusingly similar to any existing registered name, protected mark, or international agency designation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant, through its licensed registered agent, may file a written administrative appeal with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice. The appeal must state the grounds for reconsideration, provide supporting evidence of distinctiveness, and list at least two alternative names. The Registrar will issue a written decision within 21 calendar days. A rejected name based on a prior valid reservation or a protected statutory token cannot be appealed; applicant may submit a new name reservation immediately after the appeal period lapses or earlier if the Registrar grants expedited review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for this non-license, low-risk novelty goods trading activity only when supported by a licensed Marshall Islands registered agent maintaining a physical office in Majuro that can accept service of process and maintain corporate records. A post-office box address alone is not compliant. The entity must maintain at least the minimum records and corporate formalities required under the Business Corporations Act.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low likelihood for this industry classification, estimated at approximately 5-10% annually. Unannounced physical on-site inspections are rare but may occur if the registered agent is audited, if AML/CFT risk indicators escalate, or if the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit issues a targeted examination request.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCCA), as amended; applicable sections include § 39 (Certificate of Incorporation), § 47 (Directors), § 118 (Registered Office and Registered Agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, National Registrar, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a Business Corporation may be formed with one share of no par value. No paid-up capital deposit, escrow, or notarization requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that upon filing of the Certificate of Incorporation, the corporation shall issue ________ shares of no par value common stock to the subscribers listed in the share register, full subscription payment being acknowledged; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office shall be maintained at [address], with [registered agent] as registered agent in the Marshall Islands; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [name] is appointed President, [name] Treasurer, and [name] Secretary, each to serve until the next annual meeting; RESOLVED FURTHER, that officers are authorised to open bank accounts, approve payment rails, and execute all certificates and filings necessary to conduct the corporation's lawful business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance (Online Corporate Registry Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability search through the authorised registered agent or the online portal using the proposed corporate name. Up to three alternative names may be submitted in order of preference. The name must end with 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an approved abbreviation and must not be deceptively similar to an existing registered entity.
required_dossiers: Preferred corporate name (up to three alternatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as deceptively similar or prohibited, an alternate name from the same reservation request will be considered; if all are rejected, a fresh application may be filed with renumbered preferences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original Certificate of Incorporation in English through the appointed Marshall Islands registered agent. The certificate must state the corporation name, authorised share structure, registered agent name and registered office address, incorporators' names and signatures, and the mandatory limitations on corporate purposes. The filing fee is paid at the time of submission.
required_dossiers: Consent of registered agent to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or requisition, submit a corrective amendment or supplemental certificate within 30 days, cure the noted defect, and re-file the certificate; any excess filing fee paid is applied to the corrected submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Registered Agent Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure that the registered agent in the Marshall Islands has signed the consent and that the registered office address is a physical street address in Majuro or another approved location. No national of the Republic is required as director or officer, but the registered agent must be an entity authorised to act as a registered agent in the Marshall Islands.
required_dossiers: Registered agent licence or authority proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or is disqualified, appoint a replacement agent within 30 days by filing a Statement of Change of Registered Agent or Registered Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of the First Board Resolution and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Company Secretary (internal corporate record)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the initial organisational meeting or execute unanimous written consent in lieu of meeting. The first board resolution must provide for the issuance of shares to founding subscribers, adoption of the registered office and agent, appointment of the initial officers, opening of bank accounts, and approval of the authorised signatories on the payment rails (SWIFT/TT and platform payment accounts). Minutes or written consents must be retained in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Meeting waiver or unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer cannot serve, the remaining directors may elect a replacement by majority written consent; if the registered agent rejects the resolution form, revise the drafting and re-execute with conformed signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Status and Tax Exemption Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the corporation is owned by non-residents and does not earn income from sources within the Marshall Islands, file the non-resident domestic corporation status application. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, a certificate of good standing, a declaration that the corporation will not conduct business or hold real property in the Republic, and pay the applicable annual franchise/licence fee. Once approved, the corporation receives a non-resident status certificate confirming exemption from Marshall Islands income tax.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar
Annual franchise or licence fee remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Revenue and Taxation Division disputes the exemption, provide further evidence of sole non-resident operations and absence of local-source income; if the status is denied, appeal to the Minister of Finance within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a non-resident Business Corporation; the registered entity does not maintain a manufacturing premise or physical place of business in the Marshall Islands. If an on-shore facility is later established, the RMI Environment Protection Authority (RMI-EPA) and the Majuro Municipal Infrastructure Office would be the competent authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No RMI industrial operating licence required for the non-resident business corporation; any physical manufacturing operation outside the Republic must comply with the licensing and food-contact safety regulations of the host manufacturing jurisdiction.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not triggered by formation of the non-resident corporation; a Full EIA Report would be required only if a compression-molding factory is established within the Marshall Islands.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If an on-island facility is proposed, the operator must comply with RMI-EPA Clean Water and Solid Waste Regulations: wastewater pH within 6.0–9.0, 5-day biological oxygen demand (BOD5) not exceeding 50 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 50 mg/L, no untreated volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in vented air, and silicone scrap disposed only at an approved solid waste facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to the non-resident formation. Should a physical workplace be opened in the Marshall Islands, the site must obtain a structural load inspection certificate and fire safety clearance from the Majuro Fire and Rescue Authority, and an occupational health clearance from the RMI Occupational Health and Safety Office before commencing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Office (RTO), Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; no dedicated electronic filing portal for non-resident business corporations, statutory filings are lodged through registered agents; official government portal: https://www.rmiembassyus.org
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident business corporation obtains its statutory corporate registration number from the Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, upon incorporation under the Business Corporations Act. No separate TIN or VAT ID is issued by the Revenue and Taxation Office because the entity is outside the Marshall Islands income tax net unless it engages in local business activity. If a local gross receipts tax filing becomes necessary, the registered agent applies to the RTO for a taxpayer identification number using form TIN-01; no social security number or employer identification equivalent is required for pure non-resident status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A corporation may elect to be a Non-Resident Domestic Business Corporation under the Non-Resident Domestic Business Corporations Act 1990, which effects tax-exempt status for foreign-source income, no withholding taxes, and no capital gains tax. No check-the-box election exists under Marshall Islands law, and hybrid mismatch elections are not recognised. The non-resident election is irrevocable except upon conversion to a resident domestic corporation, which triggers standard gross receipts tax exposure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None (no VAT, GST, or sales-and-use-tax regime); the only contextual indirect taxes are customs import duty and excise taxes under the Customs and Excise Act 1993, applicable solely to goods imported into the Marshall Islands.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable for VAT/GST; no turnover threshold exists because no such tax is imposed. A gross receipts tax registration obligation arises only when a corporation is engaged in trade or business within the Marshall Islands, with a zero-dollar threshold, i.e., any local taxable business activity triggers registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-to-tax-administration integration, or digital stamping regime exists. Commercial invoices and standard customs declarations satisfy documentation requirements; there is no pre-clearance fiscal validation for exports or sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable – the Marshall Islands does not impose VAT or GST, so no 0% export VAT rate can be claimed and no VAT refund mechanism exists. Sales of goods or services by a non-resident domestic business corporation derive from foreign-source activity and are outside the Marshall Islands gross receipts tax. If goods were physically exported from the Marshall Islands, they are not subject to any Marshall Islands indirect tax and therefore require no zero-rating substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Completed RMI Customs Export Declaration (Form CED-1)
Commercial invoice with country-of-origin and harmonized tariff classification
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT advice for export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback is possible in the absence of VAT. However, fraudulent customs declarations or deliberate misstatement of the non-resident status attract customs penalties under the Customs and Excise Act 1993, including fines up to USD 10,000 or the value of the goods, forfeiture of goods, and criminal liability for responsible corporate officers. Misuse of the non-resident election can lead to retroactive reassessment of gross receipts tax at 3% of local gross revenue, monthly interest at 1%, and a civil penalty of up to 25% of the underpaid tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) has no domestic central bank and does not issue a national currency. The U.S. Dollar (USD) is the sole legal tender and official currency pursuant to the Compact of Free Association with the United States; monetary policy is therefore determined by the U.S. Federal Reserve. Supervisory authority over licensed banking entities is vested in the Banking Commission within the RMI Ministry of Finance, operating under the Banking Act 1990 (as amended). The Ministry of Finance acts as the de facto exchange control authority; however, RMI maintains a fully liberalized currency and capital account regime with no exchange-control legislation in force.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: USD is fully and freely convertible in RMI for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no statutory restrictions on the purchase, holding, or outward remittance of foreign exchange; no government approval is required for dividend distributions, loan repayments, or capital repatriation by a non-resident Business Corporation. No withholding taxes, capital gains taxes, or remittance taxes are imposed by RMI on non-resident corporations, which simplifies profit repatriation. The practical convertibility hurdle is not legal but rather correspondent-banking compliance: Pacific-region banks face U.S. OFAC sanctions screening and global de-risking pressure, so the treasury must maintain immaculate transaction narratives, full UBO documentation, and a consistent trade-payment audit trail to prevent wire rejections or account freezes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline exists under RMI law. The non-resident Business Corporation may retain 100 percent of export proceeds in USD or any foreign currency, with no forced conversion ratio and no central-bank registration of export invoices. RMI imposes no deadline for bringing export earnings onshore. Nevertheless, the bank will independently require the retention of commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and shipping records for a minimum of five years to satisfy AML/CTF obligations and U.S. correspondent-bank audit standards. These records must be stored in a documentary compliance folder, prepared to be produced at the bank's request without delay.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (USD) and Operational Settlement Account (USD) with SWIFT/MT103 capability

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam - Republic of the Marshall Islands Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account with trade finance, commercial L/C, and cross-border wire facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low. RMI has no domestic electronics-money-institution (EMI) licensing framework; the Banking Act 1990 does not recognize EMI or payment-service-provider categories. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Mercury, Airwallex) operate solely under their home-jurisdiction licenses (UK FCA, Lithuanian NBM, U.S. state MTLs) and are not authorized or supervised by the RMI Banking Commission. Practical constraints are severe: (a) most EMIs reject RMI-domiciled entities in their onboarding jurisdiction lists; (b) the RMI's FATF/Egmont risk profile and association with offshore corporate registries trigger automatic enhanced due diligence; (c) EMIs require a physical operational address in an approved country and typically do not accept registered-agent addresses. Recommendation: use fintech rails only as an auxillary payout engine after the two domestic banking relationships are operational, and never as the primary clearing artery. Navigation into a U.S.-chartered digital bank may be attempted only after the entity obtains a U.S. EIN and presents a substantive U.S. revenue contract; even then, expect automatic decline unless a personal guarantee from a U.S.-resident signatory is offered.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At Bank of Marshall Islands (BMI), physical presence of at least one director or a formally appointed representative holding a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney is required for the initial interview at the Majuro head office. BMI does not accept default video-only KYC. At Bank of Guam - RMI Branch, a remote video interview is permitted, but the bank requires a physical branch visit by the beneficial owner or a director within twelve months of opening; the video interview must be supplemented with notarized copies of passport, proof of address, and a board resolution approving the account. For this entity, the recommended mandate is to arrange a physical meeting in Majuro within 90 days of incorporation for the UBO and one director, with the registered agent present, to satisfy the strictest requirement and eliminate potential rejection. This physical appearance should be documented with a bank-issued meeting certificate and retained in the treasury compliance file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Business Corporation with foreign beneficial owners - RMI's offshore registry profile raises shell-company opacity risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing from the RMI Registrar of Corporations, apostilled; (b) Beneficial Ownership Declaration naming all shareholders with >10% interests; (c) passport copies of all UBOs, notarized and apostilled; (d) bank reference letter from each UBO's home bank, dated less than 6 months before submission; (e) a corporate organization chart from each UBO to the BC; (f) 6 months of business correspondence including executed purchase orders from U.S./EU distributors of silicone fidget toys.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt status flagged as potential tax evasion or round-tripping conduit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) statutory tax-exemption letter issued by the RMI Ministry of Finance confirming the non-resident BC's exemption; (b) a legal opinion from a licensed RMI attorney explaining the applicable Income Tax Act provisions; (c) substantive business evidence: supply agreement with the Chinese compression-molding factory, ISIC 3240 product invoices, and US CPSC compliance certificates; (d) UBO's foreign tax-residency certificate to disprove round-tripping.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Physical-presence gap - no office, no employees, no local infrastructure in RMI.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) executed registered-office/registered-agent agreement with a licensed RMI agent; (b) documented physical-visit itinerary and bank meeting attendance record; (c) a business-continuity and premises plan; (d) letter from the licensed agent confirming local register maintenance; (e) photographs of the registered office during the physical visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Origin-of-funds risk for the capital escrow contribution from a non-OECD or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) sending-bank KYC certificate and account-statement origin of the wire; (b) source-of-wealth declaration with supporting salary slips, dividend vouchers, or asset-sale contracts; (c) if funded via shareholder loan, an executed loan agreement with interest rate and repayment schedule; (d) certified true copy of the SWIFT MT103 with narrative field explicitly stating: 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION FOR SILICONE FIDGET TOY EXPORT VENTURE'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry misclassification - 'toy' products may be auto-screened as gambling devices or adult novelty goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) product specification sheet confirming food-grade silicone (FDA 21 CFR 177.2600 compliant) tactile fidgets; (b) HS classification certificate (HS 3926.90 / HS 9503.00); (c) U.S. CPSC Children's Product Certificate and third-party lab test report showing lead, phthalate, and BPA compliance; (d) manufacturer declaration that goods contain no gaming, gambling, or adult functions; (e) end-customer distribution agreement with a mainstream U.S. toy distributor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire protocol: the shareholder remits USD via SWIFT MT103 from their foreign bank to the BC's USD account at Bank of Marshall Islands or Bank of Guam - RMI Branch. The instruction must include: (1) beneficiary account name exactly matching the register: 'Marshall Islands Business Corporation MH_BC'; (2) narrative field 72 with '//REC/NO ADVISORY' and purpose text: 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION PER RESOLUTION 2025-001'; (3) a pre-funding compliance package filed with the receiving bank: board resolution authorizing the account, share subscription letter, register of shareholders, and a capital-purpose declaration. The receiving bank will route via its U.S. correspondent (Bank of America or Citibank for BMI; Bank of Guam's correspondent network for the RMI branch). Funds enter a Capital Escrow Account and are held until the share certificate is issued by the RMI Registrar; then an internal journal transfer to the Operational Account occurs with narrative 'RELEASE OF CAPITAL AFTER CERTIFICATION'. If the originating jurisdiction is Hong Kong or mainland China, the route must be through CHATS or CIPS with an arm's length USD/CNH conversion at the shareholder's bank; private money-corridor transfers are strictly prohibited. The bank retains a post-credit file including the MT103, exchange-rate record, and compliance approval, which will also satisfy any future correspondent-bank audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier payments in China, the default rail is a SWIFT MT103 US-dollar wire to the supplier's account at a Chinese bank (through CHIPS/Fedwire for USD clearing). Wire narrative must state: 'INVOICE [NUMBER], FOOD-GRADE SILICONE FIDGET TOYS 339930/ISIC3240, EXW [FACTORY]'. If the supplier requires CNY, the treasury converts USD to CNH via the bank's FX desk and remits through CNAPS/CIPS using the same narrative. For high-value purchase orders above USD 250,000, use a commercial Letter of Credit (L/C at sight) issued by Bank of Guam - RMI Branch in favor of the Chinese supplier, advised through the supplier's bank (e.g., Bank of China Shanghai), with settlement via SWIFT MT700/MT103 matching the documentary draft, commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading. Inbound collections from U.S. and EU distributors arrive by MT103 to the operational account; treasury performs a daily cash sweep and centralizes balances, converting excess USD into EUR or CNY only where a committed 30-day payable exists. All disbursements exceeding USD 100,000 require two authorizers and a schedule submitted two banking days in advance. A monthly reconciliation of MT103 records against the ERP cash module is mandated and retained as an audit artifact.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNY Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - standard 1M/3M/6M tenors, executed with Bank of Guam's offshore FX desk or a U.S. prime broker; used to hedge CNY-denominated factory raw-material purchases and supplier disbursements.
USD/CNH Cross-Currency Swaps - plain-vanilla fixed-for-fixed swaps matching monthly trade-finance facility notional; permissible under RMI law and cleared via the bank's offshore branch.
EUR/USD Outright Forwards - used to hedge EU distributor receivables invoiced in EUR but collected in USD; tenors matched to the invoicing cycle.

Plain-vanilla FX Options (EUR/USD and USD/CNY calls/puts) - permissible for hedging competitive tender flows where retaining upside is desired; subject to the Board's Treasury Risk Management Policy with documented trade rationales.

USD Interest-Rate Swaps - permissible but not recommended at this stage unless the escrow term-deposit balance exceeds USD 1,000,000; no domestic interest-bearing asset base currently justifies the swap.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Report (Annual Report of Business Corporation under Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, Section 103)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Marshall Islands Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year; not based on incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file and pay by March 31 renders the corporation delinquent; the Registrar may assess late penalties, suspend corporate powers, and after continued default administratively dissolve or strike off the entity from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent and Registered Office Confirmation (attached to or incorporated in the Annual Franchise Tax Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations / licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 concurrently with the annual franchise tax report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete agent information causes the annual report to be deficient, exposing the corporation to delinquency procedures and potential administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Director, Officer, and Shareholder Register Current-Cycle Verification (not separately filed; maintained at the registered office for Registrar inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records held at the registered office; inspected by the Registrar upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate filing deadline; must be accurate and current as of the annual report date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Knowingly false statements in the annual report subject officers to fines and personal liability; ongoing non-maintenance supports deregistration actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to non-resident Marshall Islands business corporations under the BCA. An audit is required only if mandated by the company's shareholders, directors, or a court order, or if the corporation is listed on a stock exchange. The subject low-risk, non-resident fidget-manufacturing entity falls below any audit-triggering activity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Marshall Islands BCA imposes no general accounting-framework filing requirement. If financial statements are prepared voluntarily, they may follow IFRS, US GAAP, or a consistent local-GAAP-equivalent framework. No financial statements are filed with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Marshall Islands BCA requires every business corporation to maintain a registered office and resident agent and to keep statutory registers available for inspection. The registered agent must collect and maintain current beneficial ownership information as part of client due diligence. An annual confirmation of shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners is obtained by the service provider at the time of the annual report preparation; share transfers occurring during the year must be reflected in the register of members before the annual report submission.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$800 - US$2,500 per annum for licensed resident agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit required; voluntary single-entity audit typically ranges from US$3,000 - US$8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) imposes no general corporate income tax. A Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) is categorically exempt from all RMI taxes, including the Business Privilege Tax (BPT), provided it carries on no business and derives no gross revenue within RMI territory. The only in-scope levy is the 3% Business Privilege Tax on gross revenue derived from business conducted in RMI, which does not apply to an offshore compression-molding entity producing food-grade silicone tactile fidgets.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory zero-rate regime: NRDC status under the Business Corporations Act (BCCA) 1990 confers a full exemption from the BPT and any income-type tax; no capital gains tax, no dividend, interest, or royalty withholding tax, and no estate, gift, or annual wealth tax. No tax holiday application is required because the exemption is automatic upon validly holding NRDC status and maintaining an RMI registered agent. The entity is treated as tax-transparent for RMI purposes; true economic activities are taxable only in the jurisdiction of effective management if that jurisdiction asserts residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Report of a Business Corporation (BCCA Form AR) — filed in the office of the RMI Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro; submission is effected exclusively through the licensed registered agent via the RMI Corporate Registry e-portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the last day of the month in which the anniversary of incorporation occurs (e.g., an entity incorporated on 12 March files by 31 March of each year). No statutory extension is available; the government annual fee, tiered by authorized share capital, is payable concurrently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 1 — Corporate Name and Registrar File Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The exact registered name and the unique registration number appearing on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the name exactly as registered; any difference must first be cured by Articles of Amendment filed with the Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 2 — Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The RMI street address of the registered office and the name and address of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A licensed registered agent is mandatory and cannot be replaced by the company itself; non-resident shareholders and directors need not be publicly disclosed beyond the agent's KYC records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full name, residential address, and nationality of each director and officer in office at the reporting date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident natural or legal persons may serve; the registered agent must hold current proof-of-identity records under the RMI AML framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of authorized shares, par value, and the number of issued and outstanding shares at year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify against the share ledger and any share transfer records; share premium and paid-in capital must reconcile with the operating entity's bank statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a monthly penalty of 10% of the government annual fee for each month or part-month overdue, capped at 100% of the fee; certificates of good standing are withheld; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to strike the corporation off the register and administratively dissolve it, with reinstatement subject to arrears, penalties, and a reinstatement fee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Business Privilege Tax Return (BPT-1) — filed with the RMI Revenue and Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance, Majuro; e-filing through the RMI tax administration portal or paper lodgment via the registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual on a calendar-year basis, with quarterly estimated prepayments when annual RMI-source gross revenue exceeds USD 50,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual BPT-1 return due within 30 days after the close of the calendar year (December 31); quarterly prepayments due by the 20th day of the month following each calendar quarter. For the target NRDC deriving no RMI-source gross revenue, no BPT-1 is required to be filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A — Gross Revenue Derived from Business in RMI
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenues earned for work performed, services rendered, or goods sold within the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero for a pure offshore manufacturing and sales entity; attach a one-page explanation of the offshore supply chain (molding equipment, silicone goods, and platform sales) to preempt an audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule B — Related-Party Revenue and Apportionment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue derived from transactions with related persons and the basis of apportionment to RMI-source gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only if the entity maintains an RMI branch, warehouse, or sales agent; otherwise leave nil and preserve contemporaneous intercompany agreements, purchase orders, and freight documents for nexus inquiries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of Non-Resident Domestic Corporation status and certification that no business is carried on in RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must be signed by a director or authorized officer; a false declaration exposes the signatory to the evasion penalties below and to director personal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly penalty of 5% of the assessed tax for each month or part-month, capped at 50% of tax; understatement penalty of 15% for material omissions; interest accrues at 1.5% per month on arrears; willful evasion is punishable by fine of up to USD 10,000 and/or imprisonment for up to three years; the tax authority may enforce collection by distress warrant against the entity's RMI assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Economic Substance Notification Return (ESR-N1) — filed with the RMI Economic Substance Authority through the registered agent; applicable only where the entity is within the scope of the Economic Substance (Amendment) Act 2019 and the Economic Substance Regulations 2020.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months of the entity's fiscal year-end; the first filing window is determined by the RMI Registrar's published ESR schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of any of the eight ESR relevant activities: banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, distribution and service centers, or intellectual property holding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The target compression-molding and manufacturing activity is not a listed relevant activity; confirm 'not in scope' in the return where the form permits, and retain supporting operational records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the jurisdiction in which the entity is tax resident and the authority issuing the residence classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An NRDC is not tax-resident in RMI; declare the jurisdiction of effective management, attach a foreign tax residence certificate if available, and verify the substance requirements of that jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of premises, employees, and expenditure incurred in the claimed residence jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the registered lease, payroll records for operational staff, and board minutes documenting decision-making; a shell declaration risks EU blacklist countermeasures and audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the ESR return without reasonable excuse: fine of up to USD 10,000; continuing non-compliance after notice attracts a daily penalty of up to USD 2,000; the Registrar may suspend or strike the entity; directors who caused the default may be disqualified.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — RMI imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by a business corporation. A non-resident shareholder receiving distributions from the NRDC is subject to no RMI dividend tax, source tax, or remittance tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI maintains no comprehensive double-taxation agreement network. The only binding tax treaty is the United States — Republic of the Marshall Islands Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (Article 8, signed 1986, in force 1988), limited to international shipping and aircraft income derived from the other jurisdiction. Because RMI does not tax non-residents, no RMI tax-residence certificate or advance treaty-relief application exists for dividend payments. Parties seeking foreign tax credits should obtain a Certificate of Corporate Existence / Good Standing from the RMI Registrar and a tax-exemption letter from the Revenue Office; US-source shipping income is claimed via a US treaty position (IRS Form 8833 or a protective return). No TRC procedure is applicable to this entity for ordinary dividend distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 0% on both cross-border royalties and debt interest paid to non-residents — RMI levies no withholding tax on payments of any kind to non-residents. Treaty rates: the US-RMI treaty does not cover royalties or interest; therefore, payments from US sources are governed by US domestic law (the US portfolio interest exemption may apply to arm's-length interest; US royalties generally face a 30% statutory WHT absent a US treaty reduction, and no US-RMI treaty relief exists for royalty income).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: None — RMI has no transfer-pricing statute, no Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country reporting requirements, and no associated documentation threshold in USD or any other currency. The only related-party computational rule appears in the Business Privilege Tax apportionment provisions, which attribute RMI gross revenue to a permanent establishment; the BPT return obligation arises when RMI-source gross revenue exceeds USD 50,000 per annum. For the target NRDC with zero RMI-source revenue, no transfer-pricing documentation is mandated; prudent practice dictates retaining arm's-length intercompany pricing evidence to rebut any reclassification of the entity as locally taxable.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: RMI enacted the Economic Substance (Amendment) Act 2019 and the Economic Substance Regulations 2020 to address EU and OECD Global Forum concerns. The ESR applies only to an RMI tax-resident entity or an RMI permanent establishment undertaking one of eight relevant activities: banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, distribution and service centers, and intellectual property holding. A non-resident business corporation manufacturing food-grade silicone sensory fidgets entirely offshore is not within any relevant ESR category and is not RMI tax-resident. Nevertheless, the RMI remains listed on the EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions (Annex I), and its AML framework is subject to Asia/Pacific Group mutual evaluation; therefore the entity must demonstrate meaningful economic substance (leased premises, employees, local board decisions, operational bank account) in its actual management jurisdiction and furnish an ESR nil assessment letter from its registered agent to withstand enhanced due diligence by banks and counterparties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion — False Business Privilege Tax Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an RMI office, physical warehouse, or local sales force through which RMI-source gross revenue is earned, while continuing to claim the NRDC zero-rate exemption; alternatively, understating or omitting RMI-source revenue attributable to an RMI permanent establishment on a BPT-1 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of 3% BPT on the full unreported RMI gross revenue; monthly late-filing penalty up to 50% of tax; understatement penalty of 15%; interest at 1.5% per month; criminal fine up to USD 10,000 and/or imprisonment up to three years; distress warrant enforcement against the entity's local assets; loss of NRDC status and consequent revocation of the tax-exempt classification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause a false BPT-1 declaration are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax; RMI courts will pierce the corporate veil upon proof of fraud or sham; directors face criminal fines, imprisonment, asset freezes, travel bans, and disqualification from managing any RMI corporation.
